process: Build the first version with the most capable model for every step.
Run it on your real examples and record how good the results are. That is your baseline.
Before switching to a smaller model, try a lower effort setting on the same model if it offers one; that is often the better lever.
Swap in smaller, cheaper models one step at a time, keeping each swap only if quality still meets the baseline.
Judge each choice on three things: quality against your examples, cost per run, and speed.
models.examples: Examples as of October 2026; check before choosing. Start with Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic's default starting point, and use Claude Fable 5.1 only where Opus falls short. OpenAI, Google and others offer similar tiers.

why.text: A fixed workflow is predictable, but its AI steps can still make mistakes.

gotchas.title: The bill grows with use

gotchas.title: Mistakes compound

gotchas.title: Personal data can leak in output
gotchas.body: Filter output for personal information, share only what each step needs, and don't put secrets in the system prompt; prompts can be coaxed into revealing themselves.

gotchas.title: The bill grows with use

gotchas.title: It only runs on its own once it's set up to
gotchas.body: Chat and agent work are one Claude app now, and nothing happens until something starts it. gotchas.title: Don't add AI just because you can
gotchas.body: If the output is a fixed function of the input, AI adds cost and unpredictability. Vendors may pitch an AI agent for this; a plain workflow is the better buy.

gotchas.title: Airflow is a developer tool
gotchas.body: Every workflow is written in Python, compared with n8n's visual builder, and a production setup needs ongoing monitoring and tuning. Budget for someone to own it, or use a managed Airflow service.

gotchas.title: You don't need MCP here
gotchas.body: MCP is how an AI discovers and uses tools. A workflow without AI uses the workflow tool's normal app connections, which are simpler to set up and audit.

firstSteps: Write every step, rule and exception on one page, and check it against 20 recent real cases.
Build it in Airflow with a manual start button, and run it alongside the current process for two weeks before switching over.

approach.title: Plain automation. No AI needed.
approach.summary: A rules-based workflow will do this job reliably and cheaply. Adding AI would add cost and unpredictability without adding value.

why.text: You said the work follows the same steps and rules every time. When the right result always follows from the input, a fixed set of rules is the most reliable tool.
